matrix_conclusions: AI-Film maseQ uploads are 4/4 one stable response class: HTTP 200 + 647-651 bytes + strict-parse-qualified or shape-unqualified (no media UUID in the primary slot) + FAILED_AMBIGUOUS at classification time; 4/4 later resolved to EXACTLY ONE catalog media with exact content readback.
The 647 vs 651 byte spread proves the class carries variable content; byte length alone is NOT a qualifying fingerprint.
The response envelope is not universal: the 2026-10-01 Story Auto control on a different project/account received a direct-UUID envelope. Universal Google Flow upload semantics are NOT claimed.
Failure point is durable-journal-indistinguishable between 'frames unparseable' and 'UUID shape unqualified'; the live canary captures a sanitized skeleton at classification time to separate them.
Catalog visibility delay after POST is bounded under ~7.4 min in all observations; reconciliation windows must exceed that bound before exhaustion.
